description: A tool to learn about disk usage, fast!

next.name: aggregate
tip: Aggregate the consumed space of one or more directories or files.

option.name: --apparent-size
tip: Display apparent size instead of disk usage.

option.name: --count-hard-links
tip: Count hard-linked files each time they are seen.

option.name: --format
tip: The format with which to print byte counts.

next.name: binary
tip: Format sizes with binary units (KiB, MiB, ...).

next.name: bytes
tip: Show raw byte counts.

next.name: gb
tip: Always format sizes in gigabytes.

next.name: gib
tip: Always format sizes in gibibytes.

next.name: mb
tip: Always format sizes in megabytes.

next.name: metric
tip: Format sizes with metric units (kB, MB, ...).

next.name: mib
tip: Always format sizes in mebibytes.

option.name: --ignore-dirs
tip: One or more absolute directories to ignore.
They are not ignored when passed directly as input path.

option.name: --ignore-from
tip: One or more files with gitignore-style patterns, whose matches are left out of the report.
Files given later take precedence over files given earlier.

option.name: --no-sort
tip: Print paths in command-line order instead of sorting by size ascending.

option.name: --no-total
tip: Do not compute a total column for multiple inputs.

option.name: --stats
tip: Print additional statistics about the file traversal to stderr.

option.name: --stay-on-filesystem
tip: Do not cross filesystems or traverse mount points.

option.name: --threads
tip: The amount of threads to use.
Defaults to 0, meaning one thread per logical processor.
Set to 1 to use only a single thread.

next.name: completions
tip: Generate shell completions.

next.name: bash
tip: Generate completions for Bash.

next.name: elvish
tip: Generate completions for Elvish.

next.name: fish
tip: Generate completions for Fish.

next.name: powershell
tip: Generate completions for PowerShell.

next.name: zsh
tip: Generate completions for Zsh.

next.name: config
tip: Configuration related commands.

next.name: edit
tip: Open the configuration file in $EDITOR.
If the file does not exist, it will be created with default values first.

next.name: show-default
tip: Print the default configuration file.

option.name: --reset-with-default
tip: Destructively overwrite the active configuration file with the default configuration.
Local changes will be lost without option to recover.

next.name: interactive
tip: Launch the terminal user interface.
